proposals.before: Li Zhouyi then marched from Bin and Fang to relieve Qi and camped on the Sanyuan frontier; Huaiying drove him off and took Zhai prefecture on the way back.
proposals.after: Li Zhouyi then came with Fu-Fang troops to relieve Qi and camped on the Sanyuan frontier; Huaiying drove him off and took Zhai prefecture on the way back.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鄜坊 is Fu and Fang prefectures (鄜州、坊州), not Bin (邠). 以鄜坊兵 means he used Fu-Fang troops, not that he marched from Bin.

proposals.before: Huaiying took Ning, Qing, and Yan, but on the march back through Shengping Zhijun struck from cover and broke him.
proposals.after: Huaiying took Ning, Qing, and Yan, but on the march back through Shengping, Zhijun struck from cover and broke him.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place Shengping with the personal name Zhijun, which the literal translation already separates.

proposals.before: Rain stopped Xun at Leeping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Shen county, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.
proposals.after: Rain stopped Xun at Leping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Xin county, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.
proposals.reason: 樂平 is Leping, not Leeping; 莘縣 is Xin county, the standard English for the 915 campaign site, not Shen.

proposals.before: Suo Qing was profoundly filial; mourning his father he wasted away in grief, and neighbors praised him.
proposals.after: Sui Qing was profoundly filial; mourning his father he wasted away in grief, and neighbors praised him.
proposals.reason: 遂清 is the same Sui Qing named above; Suo is a mistransliteration of 遂.

proposals.before: As prefect of Zibo he went to meet his mother; when she reached the suburbs he took the reins and walked beside her carriage for miles—the whole prefecture counted it an honor.
proposals.after: As prefect of Zibo, Sui Qing went to meet his mother; when she reached the suburbs he took the reins and walked beside her carriage for miles—the whole prefecture counted it an honor.
proposals.reason: The following sentence in this translation names him Suo Qing; keep the established Sui Qing spelling and restore the subject.

proposals.before: At the Last Emperor’s accession Cunjie became co-equal of the Secretariat and was posted to Tianshang.
proposals.after: At the Last Emperor’s accession Cunjie became co-equal of the Secretariat and was posted to Tianping.
proposals.reason: 天平 is the Tianping Army, not Tianshang. The same error is in the literal line's Tianshang.

proposals.before: When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to the relief; they fought at the Huan River, and Guiba captured Kkuser's son Luoluo and gave him to the Wei garrison.
proposals.after: When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to the relief; they fought at the Huan River, and Guiba captured Keyong's son Luoluo and gave him to the Wei garrison.
proposals.reason: 克用 is Li Keyong; Kkuser is a corrupted transcription, also present in the literal field.

proposals.before: Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Xuzhou.
proposals.after: Wang Chongshi came from Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu Prefecture (Changshe / modern Xuchang), not Xuzhou 徐州.

proposals.before: When Qin Zongquan seized Xuzhou, Chongshi slipped away to Liang, followed Taizu against Cai, stormed Yan and Yanzhou, and commanded the Uproot-Mountains Army.
proposals.after: When Qin Zongquan seized Xu Prefecture, Chongshi slipped away to Liang, followed Taizu against Cai, stormed Yan and Yun, and commanded the Uproot-Mountains Army.
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture, not Xuzhou; 兗、鄆 are Yan and Yun, not Yan and Yanzhou.

proposals.before: When Taizu held Xuanyi, Huaiyu commanded the garrison at Yongcheng.
proposals.after: When Taizu held Xuanwu, Huaiyu commanded the garrison at Yongcheng.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣武 is the Xuanwu command, not Xuanyi.

proposals.before: With Taizu east against Yan and Yanzhou he broke Xu and Su.
proposals.after: With Taizu east against Yan and Yun he broke Xu and Su.
proposals.reason: Chinese 兗、鄆 are Yan and Yun (Yanzhou and Yunzhou), not Yan and Yanzhou.

proposals.before: Born Cong, he received the name Huaiyu from Taizu.
proposals.after: His original name was Cong; Taizu bestowed the name Huaiyu.
proposals.reason: 本名琮 means his original name was Cong, not that he was born Cong as a fused phrase.

decisions.reason: 鄜坊 denotes the Fu-Fang military region and its troops; the existing Bin reading confuses 鄜 with 邠. The proposed wording accurately renders 以鄜坊兵.
The comma correctly separates the place 升平 (Shengping) from the following subject 知俊 (Zhijun).

decisions.after: Rain stopped Xun at Leping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Shen County, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.
decisions.reason: 樂平 should be Leping, but the proposal wrongly changes 莘縣 to Xin County. In this Five Dynasties campaign context 莘縣 is Shen County in present-day Shandong, so the existing Shen reading must be retained.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鄩至樂平，遇雨，不克進而旋……鄩乃屯於莘縣

decisions.reason: The surrounding biography repeatedly names this man 遂清 as Sui Qing; 'Suo Qing' is an inconsistent mistransliteration.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遂清性至孝，居父喪哀毀

decisions.reason: 遂清 remains the explicit subject of the episode. Restoring Sui Qing removes ambiguity and keeps the established reading used immediately above.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遂清為母執轡行數十里

decisions.reason: The source has 天平, the Tianping military command; Tianshang is a transcription error.
克用 refers to Li Keyong, Luoluo's father. 'Kkuser' is corrupted text with no basis in the Chinese.
許州 is Xu Prefecture, centered on Changshe; Xuzhou would represent 徐州 and identifies a different place.
The proposed wording correctly distinguishes 許州 as Xu Prefecture and 兗、鄆 as Yan and Yun.
The command named in the source is 宣武, Xuanwu; Xuanyi is a different name.
兗、鄆 names Yan and Yun; expanding the second as Yanzhou duplicates Yan and mistranslates 鄆.
本名琮 explicitly says his original name was Cong. The proposed sentence is clearer and avoids the misleading compressed phrase 'Born Cong.'
